profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record in Davidson County, Tennessee is tagged simply Verizon Wireless, a name that itself points away from a commercial colocation data center and toward the radio-access and mobile-switching infrastructure Verizon operates to run its cellular network in the Nashville area. Verizon Wireless, now folded administratively into Verizon Communications broader wireless division, maintains mobile switching centers, or MTSOs, and network equipment sites in every metro area it serves, and these facilities are frequently tagged as data centers in open mapping databases because they contain server racks, switching equipment, and backup power systems even though they are not marketed or sold as colocation space. Nashville commercial data center market is well documented by third-party colocation directories, and cross-referencing those published lists of operators active in the Nashville metro area during this research did not surface any facility identified as Verizon-operated commercial colocation space, which is consistent with this record being wireless-network infrastructure rather than a colocation facility open to outside tenants. Tennessee is outside the nine-state footprint, Connecticut through Virginia plus Washington DC, where Verizon operates as the legacy incumbent local exchange carrier from its Bell Atlantic and NYNEX heritage, so a legacy regional Bell central office explanation does not fit here either. No operator fact sheet, county property record, SEC filing, or trade-press source naming this specific building as a Verizon data center was located this session, and the OSM tag itself carries no documented provenance beyond the name and a telecom=data_center classification. Readers should understand this record as most plausibly network infrastructure supporting Verizon wireless service in the Nashville area, not a confirmed commercial data center, and no capacity, square footage, tier rating, or year-built figures are asserted here because none could be verified.

reading.body:
This OpenStreetMap record is tagged as Verizon Wireless in Davidson County, Tennessee, but the name and available evidence point toward mobile-network infrastructure rather than commercial colocation space. Verizon operates mobile switching centers and network equipment sites in every metro area it serves, and these facilities contain server racks and switching gear even though they are not marketed as data center capacity available to outside tenants. Cross-referencing Nashville commercial colocation directories and checking operator fact sheets, county records, and trade press sources did not surface any Verizon-operated commercial facility at this location, which is consistent with this record documenting wireless-network infrastructure supporting Verizon's cellular service in the Nashville area.

No capacity figures, square footage, tier rating, or year-built date for this facility could be verified from published sources. The research status on this record is complete, and readers should understand this as network infrastructure rather than a confirmed commercial data center with publishable IT load. Because no published megawatt figure exists for this site, it cannot be ranked by capacity or counted toward Tennessee's commercial data center inventory.

Tennessee has 24 mapped facilities in this research, of which 4 have published megawatt figures totaling 12.13 MW. This location does not appear in that ranked set of published capacity.
